RESULT v1 | kf2ee903fc4 | RFC 793 defines the Maximum Segment Lifetime (MSL) as 2 minutes (120 seconds), a conservative upper bound meant to ensure old duplicate segments have expired before a new connection reuses the same 4-tuple. TCP mandates that a socket remain in TIME_WAIT for 2 * MSL to safely complete connection teardown. In the Linux kernel, however, this is implemented as a fixed compile-time constant rather than a runtime calculation. The constant `TCP_TIMEWAIT_LEN` is defined in net/ipv4/tcp_input.c as 60 * HZ, which yields a fixed 60-second TIME_WAIT period regardless of network conditions. This is one-third of the theoretical 2*MSL value (240 seconds) implied by RFC 793 and reflects a practical engineering trade-off favoring faster socket reuse over strict standards adherence. Administrators can override this via sysctl but not at the individual-socket level.
